result.summary: This is a wide, auto-oriented commercial corridor with multiple travel lanes and no visible pedestrian crossings. While sidewalks are present, they lack a buffer from high-speed traffic and are interrupted by numerous driveway access points.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The roadway is extremely wide with at least five lanes of traffic and no mid-block crossing or refuge island.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is directly adjacent to a travel lane with no planting strip or parked cars to protect pedestrians.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Multiple curb cuts for commercial parking lots create frequent conflict points between vehicles and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crossing with high-visibility paint and signage to alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a buffer zone with trees or bollards between the sidewalk and the roadway to improve safety and comfort.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with a large painted median but no physical protection or marked crossings. A gas station creates a significant conflict zone due to its wide, continuous curb cut, which interrupts the sidewalk and exposes pedestrians to turning vehicles. The overall design prioritizes high-speed vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety and comfort.

hazards.name: Wide Gas Station Apron
hazards.description: The continuous curb cut for the gas station creates a long, undefined conflict zone between pedestrians and vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Far side of the street, center-left

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway lacks a protected mid-block crossing or refuge, forcing pedestrians to cross a wide expanse of traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the image

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Separation
hazards.description: The painted median provides no physical barrier to protect pedestrians or slow down traffic.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Consolidate and narrow the gas station entrances to define clear pedestrian paths and reduce vehicle conflict points.

interventions.title: Raised Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Replace the painted median with a raised concrete island to provide a safe waiting area and slow traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crossing with appropriate signage or signals to facilitate safe passage across the wide arterial.

result.summary: The street environment is characterized by a wide roadway with a painted median and parallel parking, which likely encourages higher vehicle speeds. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crossings and the significant unprotected crossing distance create a hostile environment for pedestrians. The presence of street trees and lighting provides some amenity, but the overall design prioritizes vehicle throughput.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway, including travel lanes, a parking lane, and a wide painted median, creates a long unprotected distance for pedestrians to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left-center of the roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right curb block sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the curb

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Replace the painted median with a raised concrete refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to designate safe crossing locations.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, continuous sidewalk in good condition, fronted by active commercial businesses. A large street tree provides shade but, along with parked vehicles, creates minor visual obstructions, while a garage entrance introduces a point of vehicle conflict across the walkway.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict
hazards.description: A garage door indicates a vehicle access point that crosses the sidewalk, creating potential for pedestrian-vehicle collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, the white garage door and associated curb cut.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The large tree trunk and parked vehicles may obscure pedestrians from the view of drivers, particularly near the driveway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center, the white SUV and the large tree.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the garage entrance to improve sightlines between exiting drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Driveway Treatment
interventions.description: Use contrasting pavement or markings across the driveway to alert drivers they are crossing a pedestrian zone.
